findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the AC-3 grep pattern with the penalty's written form: either grep for the numeric '-0.10' (anchored, e.g. `grep -nF -- '-0.10'`) or commit the scoring bullet to the exact phrase 'minus 0.10'.
evidence: AC: "checked by `grep -n 'minus 0.10' ...verification.md` matching"
Body consistently uses '-0.10': "Only `explicit_justified` carries the **-0.10 validity penalty**", "takes the -0.10 at Phase 2"
Verify-command defect taxonomy item (1): substring / literal mismatch between the pattern and the artifact as it will actually be written
findings.finding: AC line 3 greps for the literal string 'minus 0.10', but every occurrence of the penalty in the plan body is written as '-0.10' (e.g. 'the -0.10 validity penalty', 'takes the -0.10 at Phase 2'). If the author writes the scoring bullet using the numeric form '-0.10' (as the body models), the acceptance grep will not match and the AC fails despite correct content — or the author must insert an unnatural 'minus 0.10' phrasing solely to satisfy grep.
scenarios: Author writes the scoring bullet with the numeric '-0.10' form; the grep exits non-zero and the AC is marked failed even though the penalty is documented correctly.
findings.suggested_fix: Change AC-3 to `grep -nF -- '-0.10' ...verification.md` (matching the '-0.10' form used throughout the body), or state explicitly in Edit 1 that the scoring bullet writes the phrase 'minus 0.10'.

Only the `none` value has a dedicated row check.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — the prior_decision value-coverage grep
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with four value-specific checks, mirroring the existing `| \`none\` |` row check, e.g. `grep -n '\`explicit_bare\`' ...` and `grep -n '\`incidental\`' ...` each matching.

findings.finding: The prior_decision AC uses `grep -c -E 'explicit_justified|explicit_bare|incidental|prior_decision' ... returning >= 4`, which counts matching LINES across a broad alternation and does not prove all four distinct emitted values are present — `prior_decision` alone appearing on 4+ lines satisfies it while `incidental` or `explicit_bare` could be missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with four separate matches, e.g. `grep -n 'explicit_justified' ...`, `grep -n 'explicit_bare' ...`, `grep -n 'incidental' ...`, and the existing `grep -n '| \`none\` |' ...` row all matching.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the divergence research round's behavior for survivors with no candidate move (e.g. both proposers `defer → known-debt`): either exempt them from the round or state how the symmetric questions are posed when one/both sides have no approach.
evidence: Plan (Edit 2): 'any survivor not covered by a converged move now triggers one targeted research round put symmetrically to both records — has the community explicitly rejected this project's approach, and has this project explicitly rejected the community's?'

The existing file scopes the tiebreak to moves: remediation.md:38-40 'any survivor **not covered by a converged move** sends its divergent candidate moves to a **research subagent**' — the plan drops 'divergent candidate moves' from the trigger.
remediation.md:12: 'A proposer may also return `defer → known-debt` for a real survivor with no low-risk move.' — such a survivor has no approach for the symmetric research questions to compare.
T8(d): the fallback for the no-candidate-move sub-case of the newly-broadened trigger is unspecified.
findings.finding: Edit 2 broadens the divergence-research trigger to 'any survivor not covered by a converged move' but the research round's two questions presuppose candidate approaches to test; the plan does not specify what the round does for a survivor whose only proposer output was `defer → known-debt` (no move to put to the community/project).
findings.location: Edit 2 — remediation.md, 'divergence research round' (replaces 'Finding-completeness → OSS-research tiebreak')
scenarios: Both blind proposers return `defer → known-debt` for a survivor: it is 'not covered by a converged move', so the round fires, but there is no project approach vs. community approach to bucket.
One proposer defers and the other proposes a move: the symmetric 'has the community rejected THIS PROJECT's approach' question has no project approach to name.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Edit 2: 'A survivor for which both proposers returned only `defer → known-debt` carries the defer forward unchanged and does not enter the research round (there is no approach to arbitrate); the round runs only where at least one divergent candidate move exists.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State prior_decision's fallback when its git-based queries cannot run (no/shallow git history): either add a fifth value/flag distinguishing 'could not check' from `none`, or explicitly document that the queries-cannot-run case maps to `none` (no penalty) and why that is acceptable.
evidence: Plan: prior_decision 'runs four deterministic queries (`git log -S '<symbol>' --all` ... a `git blame -L` on the range ...)' — three of four are git-dependent.
Plan value table: '`none` — the queries returned no record.' No value distinguishes 'could not run' from 'ran, found nothing'.
The skill itself documents git as optional: verification.md:189 '## Trends  (only if git history available)' and references/patterns.md:121 'concern: trends — needs git history'.

T8(d): a fallback for an incomplete/failed sub-step is unspecified — the decision rule keys the -0.10 penalty on `explicit_justified`, and a git-less repo silently degrades every finding to `none` (no penalty) without the plan saying that is the intended fallback.
findings.finding: The prior_decision check's four-value enum gives no distinct value or fallback for the case where its three git-based queries CANNOT run (repository without git history), collapsing it into `none` — the same value used for 'queries ran and found no record' — with no default stated.
findings.location: Edit 1 — verification.md, prior_decision section (four-value table); the query block `git log -S`, `git blame -L`, grep queries
scenarios: Janitor runs over a repo with no git history (or a shallow clone); every prior_decision resolves to `none` and the intent check is silently a no-op.
A symbol exists but `git log -S` returns nothing because the symbol predates the imported history — indistinguishable from a genuine 'no decision was recorded'.
findings.suggested_fix: In the prior_decision section, add a sentence: 'When git history is unavailable, run the ADR/docs and ticket-id greps only; if no record surfaces, classify `none` and note in the Phase-4 record that the git-based queries could not run — this is a no-decision-found result, not a suppressed one.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in verification.md how harm_reachable is distinguished from the existing impact_follows_necessarily (e.g. reachability of a triggering state vs. necessity of the consequence given the state), so the two do not silently double-penalize one underlying evidentiary weakness.
evidence: verification.md L38: impact_follows_necessarily — 'the asserted harm necessarily follows, not merely possibly and not contingent on a separate unlikely mistake'
Plan: harm_reachable 'requires naming a concrete triggering input or state that produces the asserted harm ("this could break" is not enough)'
Both target the same failure mode: an asserted harm that cannot be shown to actually arise
findings.finding: harm_reachable (a fifth validity sub-question requiring a named concrete triggering input/state) substantially overlaps the existing impact_follows_necessarily sub-question, so one underlying defect can incur two independent 1/5 validity deductions without the plan acknowledging or reconciling the overlap.
findings.location: Plan, Edit 1 — 'harm_reachable, a fifth validity sub-question'; verification.md L38
scenarios: A finding asserting a merely-hypothetical harm scores 'no' on BOTH impact_follows_necessarily and harm_reachable, taking 2/5 off validity for a single evidentiary weakness
